description: What a fault-tolerant quantum computer would need to run a program. First its logical counts: T gates, Toffolis, rotations (each costed at the T count of its own synthesised Clifford+T word, within its share of the budget), measurements, T depth and total depth, and logical qubits with the ancillas that gates under several controls need. Then, on a physical qubit, the planar model's code distance (the gate-based surface code's model fitted to this engine's own decoders), T factories, physical qubits and runtime, and the frontier of estimates trading qubits for time. Takes a program, or a logical-counts or routine document. Every estimate is sealed in the resource-estimate receipt family, binding the program's digest and the ε budget; the answer's notes state the model's assumptions. Quote the figures with the qubit, the budget and the clock, and call them an estimate. Sealed with the service's key; verify_quantum_receipt checks the seals and re-runs it. A program with more than 256 distinct rotation angles, or a budget too fine for its rotations, is refused with the local command.

budget.description: The probability the run may fail, shared by logical errors, distillation and the rotations' synthesis (default 1e-3).

calibration.description: The gate-based surface code's model: fitted to this engine's exact-matching decoder (default) or its union-find decoder, or the planar model's assumed one.

clock.description: How long a Toffoli takes: steps (the default: three logical steps of d cycles), or {"reaction_us": t}, the reaction-limited clock: its Clifford fixups teleported away, one tick of the control system's reaction time t µs (never shorter than a measurement on the qubit), with enough factories to keep up.

counts.description: A logical-counts document instead of a program: numQubits, tCount, rotationCount, rotationDepth, cczCount, ccixCount, measurementCount.

export.description: Also give the program's counts as a logical-counts or a routine document, under export.

max_slowdown.description: The most the frontier slows the program by to need fewer factories (default 256).

name.description: The program's name in a routine document.

qasm.description: The program, OpenQASM 3 or 2. Give this, counts or routine.

qubit.description: The physical qubit: a reference qubit (ns-e4, the default: 50 ns gates, 1e-4 error; us-* are 100 µs gates, meas-* measurement-based), or one described.

routine.description: A routine document instead of a program (version v1: routines with their ports, resources, children and connections).

name: estimate_resources

anyOf.description: A resource estimate as a host returns it (the command line's estimate --json, both servers' estimate_resources, the job service's POST /v1/estimate): the request, and the result, which its receipt seals in a job's form. The result holds the program's logical counts, the error budget and how it was shared, the decoder calibration the physical model uses, the headline estimate and the frontier trading physical qubits for runtime, each estimate sealed in the resource-estimate receipt family (the frontier's naming the headline's as parent), and the model's notes. A result names the engine that made it and this schema (engine and schema); results made before results carried them have neither. docs/estimate.md explains every number.

request.description: A program (qasm), a logical-counts document (counts) or a routine document (routine), with the estimate's options, as given.

clock.description: How long a Toffoli takes: steps (the default: three logical steps of d cycles), or the reaction-limited clock, a Toffoli one tick of the control system's reaction time in µs, its Clifford fixups teleported away, with enough factories to keep up.

calibration.description: The decoder calibration the physical model uses: the decoder, the experiment, the fit, its measured range, and how to reproduce it.

counts.description: The program's logical counts: qubits and ancillas, measurements, Clifford gates, T gates, Toffolis, rotations (each costed at its own synthesised word's T count), T states, depths.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

epsilon.description: The error budget, the synthesis share and each rotation's share, the bound the rotations' distances add to, and their T counts.

estimate.description: One estimate on a physical qubit: the code and its distance, the slowdown, physical qubits (the algorithm's and the factories'), factories, runtime, logical steps and their length, tiles, the logical error, T states, and how the budget was shared; sealed by its resource-estimate receipt (receipt), or marked the headline.

clock.description: On the reaction-limited clock only: its reaction time, one tick at this estimate's slowdown, and the Toffolis run on ticks. Then steps are the lattice-surgery steps alone, and runtime_s adds the ticks.

receipt.description: A receipt of the resource-estimate family: the estimate, the hashes of its job and its result, its Merkle root, its signer and signature, and the receipt it names as parent.

clock.description: On the reaction-limited clock only: the runtime the estimate's steps do not account for, read from its signed figures. How long one tick was is the job's, whose hash binds the reaction time.

export.description: With export: the program's counts as a logical-counts or a routine document.

frontier.description: Estimates no other beats on both physical qubits and runtime; the headline among them.

items.description: One estimate on a physical qubit: the code and its distance, the slowdown, physical qubits (the algorithm's and the factories'), factories, runtime, logical steps and their length, tiles, the logical error, T states, and how the budget was shared; sealed by its resource-estimate receipt (receipt), or marked the headline.

options.description: The options the estimate ran with, the defaults filled in.

program.description: What was estimated: a circuit (its digest, BLAKE3 of the program's text), or a document's counts.

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.
